digest.top_line: STELLAR: 5x5 Gy + CAPOX noninferior to 50 Gy/25f CRT in LARC (3yr DFS 64.5% vs 62.3%, HR 0.883), with 3yr OS 86.5% vs 75.1%.
digest.tldr: Rectal carried the day: two phase III TNT trials, both showing locoregional control is already saturated by either RT schedule (STELLAR LRR 8.4% vs 11.0%; TNTCRT 6.03% vs 6.19%), so the intensification argument lives entirely in distant failure and toxicity sequencing. Prostate was imaging, not therapy: PSMA PET signal without an established response-assessment role.

sites.intro: Both entries are PSMA PET, and both are about what the scan does NOT yet license: a natural-history cohort with no tabulated concordance, and a point-counterpoint arguing uptake tracks AR signaling rather than burden.

studies.name: PSMA-Positive BCR Natural History Study
studies.tldr: Baseline data, first 130 pts: most BCR pts with PSA doubling time >9-12mo still have PSMA PET findings when PSA >5.
details: 🔍 Prospective NCI natural history cohort; eligibility PSA ≥0.5 after definitive therapy incl. salvage RT (or declined salvage RT)
🔍 Baseline PSMA PET, then annual imaging if negative, every 6 months if anything (incl. equivocal) is seen
📊 Baseline analysis of first 130 pts; median follow-up ~2 years, study ongoing
📊 Only ~1/3 of pts have gone on therapy; the majority are observed off treatment
📊 Of the first ~150 pts, 5 have progressed on conventional imaging (Madan poster, ~1.5yr f/u)
📊 Reported that >95% have not had drastic sudden PET changes discordant with PSA/PSADT
🔍 Permitted on-study therapy is short-course only: intermittent ADT, SBRT, intermittent ARPI or Radium-223 trials, anything <6 months
🔗 Designed pre-EMBARK, so the comparator framing is observation vs intermittent therapy, not continuous ADT/enzalutamide

⚠️ No effect sizes, no concordance statistics, no denominators for the doubling-time subgroups reported in source; percentages above are the investigator's spoken figures in an interview, not tabulated results
⚠️ Interview transcript of a poster, not a peer-reviewed report; single-institution NCI cohort with trial-enriched referral pattern

verdict.rationale: Observational baseline cross-section of an ongoing cohort, no outcome endpoint reached; source is an interview, not tabulated data. Follow-up analysis pending.
verdict.audience: PSMA-positive biochemical recurrence post-definitive therapy, PSA ≥0.5, salvage…

studies.significance: The RT-relevant read is where the disease sits: prostate bed recurrence and nodal disease are the dominant PSMA findings even in PSADT >9-12mo pts, i.e. the population being sent for metastasis-directed SBRT. Only ~1/3 went on any therapy and 5/150 progressed on conventional imaging, which argues observation remains a defensible arm when weighing SBRT for a PET-only lesion.
studies.monday_clinic: In post-prostatectomy pts already salvage-irradiated who now show a PET-only node or bed lesion with slow PSADT, this supports observation as a legitimate option alongside metastasis-directed therapy; it says nothing about pts with rapid PSADT or conventionally visible metastases.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Prospective NCI **natural history** cohort of PSMA-positive biochemical recurrence, therapy not mandated. Imaging is protocolized: **baseline PSMA PET**, annual if negative, **every 6 months** if any finding including equivocal. Median follow-up ~2 years, accrual ongoing.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Recurrence after definitive therapy with **PSA ≥0.5**; post-prostatectomy pts must have had salvage radiation or declined it. The cohort is explicitly framed as **BCR, not metastatic**: none would have been eligible for metastatic trials before PSMA PET.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: No mandated therapy. Permitted on-study treatment is short-course only, **under six months**: intermittent ADT, SBRT, and intermittent ARPI or Radium-223 protocols. **About one third** have started any therapy; the majority are observed.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Baseline cross-section of the first **130 pts** relates PET findings to PSA doubling time. The **vast majority** of pts with PSADT >9 or >12 months, historically low risk, had PSMA PET findings once PSA exceeded 5: nodal disease, prostate bed recurrence, and occasional equivocal small bone lesions. No concordance statistic or per-subgroup denominator is reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents PSMA-positive BCR after definitive local therapy with salvage RT given or declined, PSA ≥0.5. Does not represent conventionally metastatic disease, de novo mCSPC, or pts who have not completed local salvage.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Beyond the immaturity, the source is a **conference interview transcript**, so every figure is spoken rather than tabulated, and the progression count (5) is drawn from a **separate poster** on a different subset with different follow-up. Single-institution NCI accrual selects for trial-willing pts, which likely inflates the observed proportion.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The framing argument is that PSMA positivity in BCR is a **new disease state**, not early mCSPC, and that treating it with doublet or triplet mCSPC regimens risks systematic overtreatment. The unresolved question is whether PET burden adds risk stratification beyond PSA doubling time; the interim follow-up analysis is stated to be in progress.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The PET findings concentrate in prostate bed and nodes, exactly the targets a rad onc is asked to treat with metastasis-directed SBRT after salvage RT has already been delivered. With ~1/3 on any therapy and 5 of ~150 progressing on conventional imaging, the data support observation as a comparator arm rather than reflexive treatment of every PET-avid lesion.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Slow PSADT no longer excludes PET positivity once PSA exceeds 5, so a positive scan alone is a weak trigger for systemic therapy. The cohort was designed pre-EMBARK and permits only short-course intermittent treatment, which frames the question as whether to start any systemic agent, not which doublet.

open_questions: Does PET burden risk-stratify beyond PSA doubling time
Which PSMA-positive BCR pts can be safely observed off therapy
Natural history of equivocal small bone lesions on PSMA PET

studies.name: USPCC 2026 Point-Counterpoint: PSMA PET as Response Assessment
studies.tldr: High δ-SUVmax on serial 18F-DCFPyL PET carried OS HR 5.03 (DPSM) and 9.31 (DASM), but uptake tracks AR signaling, not burden.
details: 🔍 Point-counterpoint talk (Rowe, UT Southwestern) arguing PSMA PET is not yet a response-assessment tool
🔍 Core biologic claim: PSMA expression is dynamically AR-regulated, not a static marker of tumor burden
📊 Zukotynski prospective single-arm series, n=16 evaluable: median time to therapy change 9.6 mo (95% CI 6.9-14.2)
📊 Same series: median OS 28.6 mo (95% CI 18.3-NA); imaging pre-ARSI and 2-4 mo after start

details.text: 📊 Uptake-change stratifiers vs outcomes (18F-DCFPyL, n=16, abiraterone or enzalutamide)

details: 📊 Mixed but predominantly increased uptake pattern tracked shorter time to therapy change and shorter OS
📊 Bipolar androgen therapy series (n=6): 3 progressed on PSMA PET at 3 mo, earlier than conventional imaging
🔍 RECIP 1.0 pairs PSMA PET with CT to call CR / PR / SD / PD after radioligand therapy; validation pending
⚠️ Repeatability work (Bland-Altman, ICC, within-subject CV) shows lesion identification and segmentation vary on serial scans
⚠️ Repeatability analyses were restricted to lesions >1.5 cm³, so small-lesion measurement error stays uncharacterized
⚠️ Evidence base is two tiny series (n=16, n=6); OS HR CIs span 1.17-21.65 and 1.81-47.87
studies.significance: Uptake change after an ARSI start is prognostic, not volumetric: high δ-absolute SUVmax carried OS HR 9.31 (95% CI 1.81-47.87). For metastasis-directed RT, a PSMA PET obtained 2-4 months into androgen-axis therapy can shift lesion conspicuity, so target selection off a post-treatment scan is not equivalent to a baseline one.
studies.monday_clinic: In mCRPC pts starting abiraterone or enzalutamide, a rise in PSMA uptake on a 2-4 month restaging PET is prognostic (shorter time to therapy change and OS) rather than a validated response measure, and it does not speak to post-radioligand-therapy assessment, where RECIP 1.0 remains unvalidated.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Point-counterpoint presentation in the USPCC 2026 PSMA PET imaging session, arguing the **negative position**. Evidence cited is a prospective single-arm 18F-DCFPyL trial (**n=16 evaluable**, imaged pre-ARSI and 2-4 mo after), a bipolar androgen therapy series (**n=6**), repeatability analyses, and the RECIP 1.0 framework.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents mCRPC (APMR) pts undergoing serial PSMA PET around an androgen-axis therapy start or bipolar androgen therapy. Does not represent response assessment after radioligand therapy, where **RECIP 1.0** is the proposed framework and validation is still outstanding.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Both cited series are small and single-arm, and the OS hazard ratios carry very wide intervals (**1.17-21.65** for DPSM, **1.81-47.87** for DASM), so the point estimates are unstable. Repeatability analyses were limited to lesions **>1.5 cm³**, leaving segmentation error in small lesions unmeasured.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Take-home points: androgen-targeted therapy has **unpredictable effects on PSMA expression**, questions remain about the robustness of uptake and reliability of lesion identification, and the field needs the **kinetics** of androgen-axis effects plus **AI-assisted lesion detection** and standardized image analysis before serial PSMA PET becomes a response measure.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Bears on metastasis-directed RT target selection: a PSMA PET taken 2-4 months into an ARSI can change lesion conspicuity through AR signaling rather than burden, so lesions picked off a post-treatment scan may not match a baseline read. Segmentation variability was only characterized for lesions >1.5 cm³.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Serial δ-SUVmax stratified outcomes on abiraterone or enzalutamide (time to therapy change 12.2 vs 6.5 mo, p=0.0001; OS 37.2 vs 17.8 mo, p=0.02), so it reads as prognostic. It is not a validated basis for switching therapy off an imaging change alone.

open_questions: Kinetics of androgen-axis effects on PSMA expression
Validation of RECIP 1.0 outside radioligand therapy
Repeatability thresholds for serial SUVmax-based response calls

sites.intro: Two phase III TNT trials, one testing short-course 5x5 and one testing doublet chemo around long-course RT, both leaving locoregional failure untouched.

studies.name: STELLAR
studies.tldr: 3yr DFS 64.5% vs 62.3%, HR 0.883 noninferior for 5x5 Gy + CAPOX vs 50Gy/25f CRT in LARC.
details: 🔍 Multicenter open-label phase III, N=599, 16 Chinese hospitals, 1:1, NI margin HR 1.43; median f/u 35.0mo
🔍 Distal/middle-third rectal adenoca, cT3-4 and/or cN+, age 18-70, ECOG 0-1; 85.8% vs 83.5% stage III
📐 All pts received IMRT (unusual for this trial set); CTV covered mesorectum, presacral space, internal iliac, obturator, ischiorectal fossa; external iliac only if cT4b
📐 TNT arm: 5 Gy x 5 then 4 cycles CAPOX, TME 6-8wk later, then 2 CAPOX. CRT arm: 50 Gy/25f + capecitabine 825 mg/m2 BID, TME, then 6 CAPOX
📊 3yr OS 86.5% vs 75.1%, HR 0.67 (0.46-0.97), log-rank P=.033, a secondary endpoint in a NI trial
⚠️ OS gain rests on 47 vs 63 deaths and no OS subgroup was significant except cT4 (HR 0.362, 0.152-0.859) and ≤5cm from verge (HR 0.540, 0.318-0.916); Polish II's early OS benefit vanished by 8yr
📊 pCR + sustained cCR 21.8% TNT vs 12.3% CRT (P=.002); cCR on re-evaluation 11.1% vs 4.4%
⚠️ Acute grade III-V toxicity 26.5% vs 12.6% (P<.001), driven by hematologic G3-4 15.8% vs 2.0%
⚠️ Preop full-dose completion 74.8% TNT vs 93.2% CRT (P<.001); RT itself was completed by every TNT pt without dose reduction

details.text: 📊 Acute grade 3-4 toxicity during preoperative treatment, TNT vs CRT

details: 🔗 vs RAPIDO and PRODIGE 23: those cut 3yr DM significantly, STELLAR and Polish II did not; STELLAR LRR 8.4% sits in the RAPIDO/PRODIGE range (4%-8.3%), well under Polish II (21%-22%)
🔗 Surgical morbidity was flat: grade III+ complications 14.0% vs 15.7% (P=.625); R0 91.5% vs 87.8% (P=.189)

verdict.rationale: Prespecified NI primary met in an adequately powered phase III, consistent with RAPIDO and Polish II. OS is a secondary endpoint at 35mo f/u, not the claim.
verdict.audience: Distal/mid-third rectal adenocarcinoma, cT3-4 and/or cN+, age 18-70, ECOG 0-1

studies.significance: Every pt got IMRT, the only trial in this set that did, and LRR was 8.4% at 3yr, so 5x5 Gy delivered with modern planning holds local control against 50 Gy/25f. The added grade 3-4 burden is hematologic (15.8% v 2.0%), from CAPOX not the RT, which shifts the 5x5-vs-long-course choice to chemo tolerance rather than pelvic dose.
studies.monday_clinic: In cT3-4 or node-positive distal/mid rectal cancer where the goal is shortening pelvic RT and front-loading chemotherapy, this supports 5x5 Gy plus CAPOX as an alternative to long-course chemoradiation; it does not extend to upper-third tumors, pts over 70, or those needing a cCR-driven watch-and-wait pathway as the primary aim.

primary_endpoint.name: 3-year disease-free survival
primary_endpoint.stat_detail: HR 0.883, one-sided 95% CI to 1.11, P<.001 noninferiority

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicenter **open-label randomized phase III**, 1:1, 16 hospitals across 11 provinces of China, enrolled Aug 2015 to Aug 2018. **N=599** (TNT 302, CRT 297), stratified by location, clinical stage and MRF status. **Noninferiority margin HR 1.43**, one-sided alpha 0.05, median follow-up **35.0 mo**.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Age 18-70, ECOG 0-1, **cT3-4 and/or node-positive** rectal adenocarcinoma of the **distal or middle third** only, no distant metastases and no prior anticancer treatment. Staging was central high-resolution MRI read by three radiologists. Stage III in 85.8% v 83.5%; **MRF involved in 56%** of both arms; cT4 15.9% v 12.8%.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: TNT arm: **5 Gy x 5** over one week. CRT arm: **50 Gy in 25 fractions** over 5 weeks with concurrent capecitabine. **All patients received IMRT**, in contrast to RAPIDO, Polish II and PRODIGE 23. CTV covered mesorectum, presacral space, internal iliac, obturator and ischiorectal fossa, external iliac only for cT4b; superior border the sacral promontory, inferior border 2-3 cm below the tumor, CTV to PTV expansion 0.5-1.0 cm.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: TNT: four cycles of **CAPOX** (oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 d1, capecitabine 1,000 mg/m2 BID d1-14) starting 7-14 days after RT, then TME, then two more CAPOX. CRT: concurrent **capecitabine 825 mg/m2 BID**, then TME, then six CAPOX. TME was recommended **6-8 weeks** after preoperative treatment in both arms; watch-and-wait was permitted on cCR or patient request.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: 3-year DFS** (locoregional failure, distant metastasis, second primary or death from any cause). Secondary: OS, MFS, LRR, surgical complications, toxicity and completion rate, plus pCR and sustained cCR.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Noninferiority confirmed: the upper bound of the DFS HR (1.11) sat below the 1.43 margin. **LRR and MFS were flat between arms**; OS favored TNT as a secondary endpoint. Complete response (pCR plus sustained cCR) was **21.8% v 12.3%, P=.002**, and 9.4% v 3.4% went to nonoperative management.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Preoperative grade III-V toxicity **26.5% v 12.6% (P<.001)**, almost entirely **hematologic** (G3-4 15.8% v 2.0%; thrombocytopenia 11.1% v 0.7%). Pelvic toxicity was closer: G3-4 proctitis 4.7% v 3.1%, diarrhea 6.4% v 4.8%. Grade III+ surgical complications 14.0% v 15.7% (P=.625), no 30-day postoperative deaths. Adjuvant-phase grade III-IV toxicity was **lower** with TNT, 3.3% v 11.8% (P=.003). Late toxicity and QoL not yet reported.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Third RCT of short-course RT plus chemotherapy vs long-course CRT. LRR 8.4% matches **RAPIDO and PRODIGE 23 (4%-8.3%)** and beats **Polish II (21%-22%)**. Unlike RAPIDO and PRODIGE 23, STELLAR showed **no 3-year DM reduction** (22.8% v 24.7%). The OS signal mirrors Polish II, whose OS advantage **disappeared at 8 years**.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents cT3-4 or node-positive adenocarcinoma of the distal and middle third of the rectum in pts age 18-70 with ECOG 0-1. Does not represent upper-third rectal tumors, pts over 70, unresectable fixed T4 disease of the Polish II type, or those with prior anticancer treatment.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Median 35 mo is short for an OS claim, and the authors note the OS benefit needs 5-10 year follow-up given the Polish II reversal. The trial is entirely Chinese with a median age of 55, roughly a decade younger than Western LARC cohorts, and the NI margin of 11% absolute was chosen for feasibility; the authors themselves say a narrower margin would have been defensible. Late toxicity and QoL are unreported, so the chief long-term tradeoff of 5x5 Gy is still open.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The trial answers a logistics question as much as an oncologic one: one week of RT plus front-loaded chemo delivers the same 3-year DFS and local control as five weeks of chemoradiation with better adjuvant-phase completion (60.0% v 48.3%, P=.009). What it does not do is reproduce the distant-control gain of RAPIDO, which used 8-12 cycles of induction chemo against STELLAR's four.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: All pts got IMRT, unique among the four TNT RCTs, and 3yr LRR was 8.4% v 11.0% with identical elective nodal coverage in both arms, so the fractionation change did not cost local control. The added grade 3-4 toxicity was hematologic (15.8% v 2.0%), not pelvic (proctitis 4.7% v 3.1%), so 5x5 Gy is defensible where chemo tolerance permits.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Four cycles of neoadjuvant CAPOX after 5x5 Gy carried the grade 3-4 burden (hematologic 15.8% v 2.0%) but bought better adjuvant-phase completion (60.0% v 48.3%, P=.009) and lower adjuvant toxicity (3.3% v 11.8%). Unlike RAPIDO's 8-12 cycles, four cycles did not cut 3yr DM (22.8% v 24.7%), so intensity, not sequence alone, looks like the lever.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: TME timing shifted (median 21 weeks from RT start in TNT v 14 weeks in CRT) without penalty: R0 91.5% v 87.8% (P=.189), grade III+ complications 14.0% v 15.7% (P=.625), no 30-day deaths, and hospital stay 8 days in both arms. Sustained cCR sent 9.4% v 3.4% to nonoperative management, enlarging the organ-preservation conversation.

open_questions: Does the 3yr OS advantage survive 5-10 year follow-up
Late toxicity and QoL after 5x5 Gy plus CAPOX
Optimal number of neoadjuvant chemotherapy cycles after short-course RT

studies.name: TNTCRT
studies.tldr: 3yr DFS 74.8% vs 66.0%, HR 0.674 (0.489-0.929), P=.016 for doublet TNT with LCRT vs nCRT in high-risk LARC.
details: 🔍 Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, N=458 (232 doublet-LC TNT vs 226 nCRT); enrolled Jun 2017 to Dec 2023; median f/u 51mo
🔍 Eligibility: stage II/III LARC, age 18-70, ≥1 MRI high-risk feature (cT4a-b, cN2, MRF involvement, or cT3c-d with EMVI)
🔍 Baseline high-risk burden: cT4 47.82%, cN2 75.98%, threatened MRF 70.96%, EMVI 54.80%
💊 Doublet arm sequencing: 1 cycle induction CAPOX → LCRT with 2 cycles concurrent CAPOX → 3 cycles consolidation CAPOX → TME
💊 Control arm: LCRT with concurrent capecitabine → TME → 6 cycles adjuvant CAPOX starting 4-8wk post-op
⚠️ RT dose, fractionation, and target volume not reported in source text; both arms used long-course RT, so the randomized variable is the concurrent/sequential chemo, not the RT
📊 Locoregional failure identical between arms: 6.03% vs 6.19%, P=.943; the DFS gain is distant-only (MFS 77.7% vs 67.6%, HR 0.655 [0.469-0.915])
📊 3yr OS 90.2% vs 87.5%, P=.167, not significant
🔍 ~87% (doublet) vs ~90% (nCRT) proceeded to TME
⚠️ Neoadjuvant-phase G3/4 AEs 27.59% vs 8.56%, P<.001, but whole-course severe toxicity 28.02% vs 24.32% (P=.371): the toxicity is front-loaded, not added
⚠️ Age capped at 70; benefit-risk in older pts untested (author-stated limitation)
🔗 Sits alongside RAPIDO, PRODIGE-23, STELLAR as TNT vs nCRT; no head-to-head vs short-course RT or non-doublet-concurrent TNT regimens

verdict.rationale: Randomized phase 3, primary DFS endpoint met, 51mo median f/u. Aligns with RAPIDO/PRODIGE-23/STELLAR TNT direction rather than contesting it; OS not significant.
verdict.audience: High-risk stage II/III LARC, age ≤70, ≥1 MRI high-risk feature…

studies.significance: Locoregional failure was 6.03% vs 6.19% (P=.943): intensifying concurrent chemo around an unchanged LCRT backbone bought nothing locally, and the entire DFS gain is metastatic (MFS 77.7% vs 67.6%). RT dose/fractionation are not in the source text. This is a chemo-sequencing decision, not an RT one.
studies.monday_clinic: In cT4/cN2/MRF-involved stage II/III rectal cancer aged ≤70, this supports moving oxaliplatin doublet in front of surgery around standard long-course chemoRT rather than to the adjuvant slot; it does not speak to pts over 70, to short-course RT schedules, or to a watch-and-wait organ-preservation goal.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicenter randomized **phase III**, N=**458**, accrual June 6 2017 to December 27 2023, median follow-up **51 months**. **Primary end point: DFS.**

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Stage II/III LARC, age **18 to 70**, with **≥1 MRI high-risk feature** (cT4a-b, cN2, mesorectal fascia involvement, or cT3c-d with extramural vascular invasion). Genuinely high-risk cohort: cT4 **47.82%**, cN2 **75.98%**, threatened MRF **70.96%**, EMVI **54.80%**.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Doublet-LC TNT: **1 cycle induction CAPOX**, then LCRT with **2 cycles concurrent CAPOX**, then **3 cycles consolidation CAPOX**, then surgery. Control: LCRT with **concurrent capecitabine**, surgery, then **6 cycles adjuvant CAPOX** at 4 to 8 weeks post-op.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **Long-course RT in both arms**, so RT is the fixed backbone and not the randomized variable. **Dose, fractionation, and target volume are not reported in the source text**, which limits transfer of the regimen to a specific local protocol.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Primary DFS met. Locoregional failure was flat (**6.03% v 6.19%**, P=.943) and 3-year OS was **90.2% v 87.5%** (P=.167), so the benefit is **distant control**, carried by MFS and pCR.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Grade ≥3 AEs during the neoadjuvant phase were higher with doublet TNT (**27.59% v 8.56%**, P<.001), but across the entire treatment course severe toxicity converged (**28.02% v 24.32%**, P=.371) and major postoperative complications were comparable (**3.98% v 2.94%**, P=.567). About **87% v 90%** underwent TME.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Extends the RAPIDO / PRODIGE-23 / STELLAR TNT signal to an uninterrupted doublet-with-LCRT schedule. The authors themselves call for comparison against **short-course RT-based** and **nondoublet-concurrent** TNT regimens, which this trial does not provide.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents MRI-defined high-risk stage II/III LARC in pts aged 18 to 70 treated with long-course RT. Does not represent pts over 70, low-risk stage II/III disease, short-course RT schedules, or a watch-and-wait organ-preservation pathway.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Adjuvant-chemo delivery in the control arm is not reported, and TNT trials typically win on completed systemic dose rather than schedule alone. OS is immature at 51 months with 3-year rates already above 87% in both arms, so the DFS-to-OS translation is unresolved.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: RT is the constant here, not the variable: both arms got long-course RT, and locoregional failure was 6.03% vs 6.19% (P=.943). Nothing in this trial supports altering dose, fractionation, or target volume (none of which the source reports); it argues for keeping LCRT while the doublet moves preoperatively.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: The randomized question is where oxaliplatin doublet goes: fully preoperative and uninterrupted (induction, concurrent, consolidation CAPOX) vs adjuvant CAPOX after surgery. Preoperative delivery bought 3yr MFS 77.7% vs 67.6% (HR 0.655) with whole-course severe toxicity comparable (28.02% vs 24.32%).
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: About 87% vs 90% reached TME and major postoperative complications were 3.98% vs 2.94% (P=.567), so the intensified neoadjuvant course did not cost resection rate or perioperative safety. pCR rose to 26.37% from 9.80%, which raises the organ-preservation conversation the authors flag as their next goal.

papers.title: Total Neoadjuvant Therapy With Long-Course Radiotherapy Versus Chemoradiotherapy in High-Risk Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (TNTCRT): A Multicenter, Randomized, Phase III Trial
papers.abstract: PURPOSE High-risk locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) carries a substantial risk of distant recurrence, which limits disease-free survival (DFS). We compared total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) integrating long-course radiotherapy (LCRT) with uninterrupted doublet chemotherapy (doublet-LC TNT) versus conventional neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT). METHODS In this multicenter, randomized, phase III trial, patients with stage II/III LARC and at least 1 high-risk feature (cT4a-b, cN2, mesorectal fascia involvement, or cT3c-d with extramural vascular invasion) were enrolled. Patients were assigned to doublet-LC TNT (induction, concurrent, and consolidation capecitabine plus oxaliplatin with LCRT) before surgery or nCRT (capecitabine with LCRT) followed by surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy. The primary end point was DFS (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03177382 ). RESULTS Between June 6, 2017, and December 27, 2023, 458 patients were randomly assigned to doublet-LC TNT (n = 232) or nCRT (n = 226). At a median follow-up of 51 months, doublet-LC TNT improved 3-year DFS (74.8% v 66.0%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.674 [95% CI, 0.489 to 0.929]; P = .016). Metastasis-free survival (MFS; 77.7% v 67.6%; HR, 0.655 [95% CI, 0.469 to 0.915]) and pathologic complete response rates (pCR; 26.37% v 9.80%; P < .001) were higher with doublet-LC TNT, whereas locoregional failure remained low and comparable (6.03% v 6.19%; P = .943). Although grade ≥3 adverse events during the neoadjuvant phase were more frequent with doublet-LC TNT (27.59% v 8.56%; P < .001), severe toxicities during the entire treatment course (28.02% v 24.32%; P = .371) and major postoperative complications (3.98% v 2.94%; P = .567) were comparable. CONCLUSION Compared with conventional nCRT, doublet-LC TNT improved DFS, MFS, and pCR rates with manageable toxicity. These findings support this intensified, doublet-based regimen as a standard option within the modern TNT paradigm. Further comparative studies are warranted to evaluate these results against other short-course radiotherapy‑based or nondoublet-concurrent TNT regimens.

papers.title: Multicenter, Randomized, Phase III Trial of Short-Term Radiotherapy Plus Chemotherapy Versus Long-Term Chemoradiotherapy in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (STELLAR)
papers.abstract: PURPOSE To ascertain if preoperative short-term radiotherapy followed by chemotherapy is not inferior to a standard schedule of long-term chemoradiotherapy in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer. MATERIALS AND METHODS Patients with distal or middle-third, clinical primary tumor stage 3-4 and/or regional lymph node–positive rectal cancer were randomly assigned (1:1) to short-term radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions over 1 week) followed by four cycles of chemotherapy (total neoadjuvant therapy [TNT]) or chemoradiotherapy (50 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks, concurrently with capecitabine [chemoradiotherapy; CRT]). Total mesorectal excision was undertaken 6-8 weeks after preoperative treatment, with two additional cycles of CAPOX (intravenous oxaliplatin [130 mg/m 2 , once a day] on day 1 and capecitabine [1,000 mg/m 2 , twice a day] from days 1 to 14) in the TNT group and six cycles of CAPOX in the CRT group. The primary end point was 3-year disease-free survival (DFS). RESULTS Between August 2015 and August 2018, a total of 599 patients were randomly assigned to receive TNT (n = 302) or CRT (n = 297). At a median follow-up of 35.0 months, 3-year DFS was 64.5% and 62.3% in TNT and CRT groups, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.883; one-sided 95% CI, not applicable to 1.11; P < .001 for noninferiority). There was no significant difference in metastasis-free survival or locoregional recurrence, but the TNT group had better 3-year overall survival than the CRT group (86.5% v 75.1%; P = .033). Treatment effects on DFS and overall survival were similar regardless of prognostic factors. The prevalence of acute grade III-V toxicities during preoperative treatment was 26.5% in the TNT group versus 12.6% in the CRT group ( P < .001). CONCLUSION Short-term radiotherapy with preoperative chemotherapy followed by surgery was efficacious with acceptable toxicity and could be used as an alternative to CRT for locally advanced rectal cancer.
